question: The grading system used by the Mughals to fix rank, salary and military responsibilities is called ___________ .
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mansabdari system.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mansabdari system:-**

 
 
• ​The Mansabdari system was introduced by Akbar for military administration and for the territorial command to sustain the parts of the army.
 
• The Mansabdari system was taken from the system followed in Mongolia.
 
• The Mughal officers whether Hindus or Muslims were given territorial commands in return for military service.
 
• They had to bring in some fixed number of men-at-arms, horses, and elephants to the field and were rated as per the numbers which were known as Zats. 
 
• 'Zat' shows the number of troops that a mansabdar was expected to maintain, while 'sawar' indicate the actual number of horses under the command of a mansabdar.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Iqta system:-**

 
 
• The Iqta system was provided institutional status by Iltutmish__.
 
• The Iqta System or Iqtadari System was introduced by Shamsuddin Iltutmish of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• It was a powerful instrument for centralization.
 
• It was based on the division of territories between Sultans and Nobility.
 
 
 
• **​Ryotwari system:-**
 
 
• Ryotwari System was introduced by Thomas Munro in 1820.
 
• First Ryotwari System was introduced in Madras.
 
• The principle was the direct collection of land revenue from each individual cultivator by government agents.
 
• The advantages of this system were the elimination of middlemen, 
 
• In this system, the Individual cultivator is called Ryot.
 
• This system was in operation for nearly 5 years.
 
 
 
• **Mahalwari system:-**
 
 
• The Mahalwari system was introduced in 1822 by Holt Mackenzie.
 
• Later, the system was reformed during the period of William Bentick in 1833.
 
• **This system divided the land into Mahals. Sometimes, a Mahal was constituted by one or more villages.**
